cases.name: ABL T315I — Imatinib resistance
cases.literature: O'Hare et al., Nat Rev Cancer 2007 — T315I drives near-total Imatinib loss in CML; >400-fold IC50 shift in cellular assays.
cases.verdict_note: Δ=+3.60 kcal/mol matches expected 'resistance' — strongest signal in the suite. Magnitude grew from +2.40 at exhaustiveness=8 to +3.60 at ex=16, consistent with reduced sampling variance unmasking the gatekeeper steric clash.

cases.name: EGFR T790M — Gefitinib resistance
cases.literature: Pao et al., PLoS Med 2005 — T790M gatekeeper drives 1st-gen TKI resistance in NSCLC.
cases.verdict_note: Δ=+1.30 kcal/mol matches expected 'resistance' — clean signal above noise floor. Was SKIP at exhaustiveness=8 (prep flake) and NOISE before that; the T790M gatekeeper resistance is now resolved.

cases.name: EGFR T790M — Osimertinib retains/gains
cases.literature: Cross et al., Cancer Discov 2014 — Osimertinib (AZD9291) retains potency against T790M; cellular IC50 ~1 nM vs T790M.
cases.caveat: Osimertinib is a covalent acrylamide on C797. Vina is non-covalent — magnitude will be smaller than IC50 shifts suggest, but the geometric T790M preference still produces a measurable ΔΔG.
cases.verdict_note: |Δ|=0.30 below ±1.0 kcal/mol noise floor — direction is slightly wrong but magnitude is sub-noise so not a credible disagreement. Covalent-mechanism case Vina was never going to fully resolve.

cases.name: BRAF V600E — Vemurafenib selectivity
cases.literature: Bollag et al., Nature 2010 — Vemurafenib (PLX4032) is V600E-selective; ~30 nM against V600E vs ~100 nM against WT BRAF in cellular assays.

cases.name: KIT D816V — Imatinib resistance
cases.literature: Heinrich et al., J Clin Oncol 2003 — D816V shifts KIT into an active conformation Imatinib cannot bind; >100-fold loss in mastocytosis.
cases.verdict_note: Δ=+2.60 kcal/mol matches expected 'resistance' — magnitude grew from +1.80 at ex=8 to +2.60 at ex=16, pattern consistent with reduced sampling variance.

cases.name: KIT D816V — Avapritinib selectivity
cases.literature: Evans et al., Sci Transl Med 2017 — Avapritinib (BLU-285) was designed to bind the D816V active conformation; sub-nM cellular potency.
cases.verdict_note: |Δ|=0.40 below ±1.0 kcal/mol noise floor — direction is wrong (expected selectivity). Avapritinib's D816V advantage comes from binding the activated conformation our 1T46 PDB is not in; rigid-receptor docking against the inactive conformation cannot capture it. Documented method limitation.

cases.name: BTK C481S — Ibrutinib covalent escape
cases.literature: Woyach et al., NEJM 2014 — C481S ablates the covalent cysteine target of Ibrutinib; >100-fold cellular IC50 loss in CLL.
cases.caveat: Ibrutinib's WT advantage is COVALENT (acrylamide → C481 thiol). Vina is non-covalent — the residual non-covalent ΔΔG should still be positive (S smaller than C, slight pocket reshape).
cases.verdict_note: Δ=+1.50 kcal/mol matches expected 'resistance' — non-covalent component of the C481S Ibrutinib loss is reliably resolved across two independent runs at different exhaustiveness.

cases.name: BTK C481S — Pirtobrutinib retention
cases.literature: Mato et al., NEJM 2021 — Pirtobrutinib is non-covalent; retains potency against C481S (cellular IC50 essentially unchanged).
cases.verdict_note: Δ=+1.80 kcal/mol DISAGREES with literature 'retained' direction
